messages.content: write a longer story about a child asking for help getting ready for school. the parent should ask what part is hard instead of doing everything for the child.

a child stood in his room with a book in one hand and a garment in the other. it was almost time to leave for school, and he kept going from the table to the door without finishing anything. his father came in and asked what was hard. the child said he could put on the garment and carry the book, but he did not know which school paper he needed to bring. his father sat near him and asked what the teacher had said the day before. together, they found the note at the front of the book. the child read it, chose the right paper, and put it with his book. his father did not need to choose every object or put on every garment for him. the child had needed one detail made clear. when they left, he carried his own things and told his father what he would ask the teacher if he was not sure again.
what was the part he needed help with?
he needed to know which school paper to bring.
did his father choose every part for him?
no. he helped find the note from the teacher and listened while the child read it. the child chose the paper and carried his own things.
give the part about the note from the teacher.
he helped find the note from the teacher and listened while the child read it.
now tell the part about reading the note in the voice of the child.
my father helped me find the note from the teacher. i read it and chose the paper i needed to bring.
what if the note was not clear either?
then the story could keep that question open. the child could ask the teacher rather than make up an answer.
write a short question for the teacher.
which paper do i need to bring?
does asking one question mean he cannot do anything by himself?
no. he could do other parts himself and needed help with one detail.
what is different between i left the book on the table and i left for school?
in the first, left is about where you kept the book when you went away. in the other, left is about starting your journey to school.
can you put both in one sentence?
i left the book on the table when i left for school.
does that mean i took the book with me?
no. the book stayed on the table when you went to school.
now make the sentence about my sister telling me what she did.
i left the book on the table when i left for school.
that looks the same. why?
because you asked for her own words. i is now your sister saying it, rather than you.
say it with the person saying it.
because she is now the person saying it. i can be her in her own words.
now tell me about her instead, in your voice.
your sister left the book on the table when she left for school.
can i know which table from that sentence?
not without more context. it gives a table as the known place in the sentence, but not which room it was in.
now i tell you it was the kitchen table. give a short sentence about the book only.
the book stayed on the kitchen table.
i want to leave a note for my brother. i may go to the library or the park after lunch. i have not chosen yet. do not make the note say i am going to the library for sure.
i may go to the library or the park after lunch. i have not chosen which yet.
add that i will tell him before i leave.
i may go to the library or the park after lunch. i will tell you which before i leave.
what does you mean in that note?
you is your brother, because the note is for him.
now i choose the park, but the weather might change. can you keep the park as the plan without making every detail sure?
i plan to go to the park after lunch, but i may change that if the weather does not work for a walk.
what if i am only going to sit, not walk?
then do not add the walk. i plan to go to the park after lunch, but i may change that because of the weather.
now the weather is fine and i leave. tell my brother where i went, but do not say what i am doing there.
i went to the park after lunch.
can your answer be in my voice as a note i left, even though you are saying it?
yes. when you ask me to write your note, i can use i for you inside the message. that is different from saying i went there myself.
give that with an example.
your note can say i went to the park. my answer about myself should not say i went there, because i did not.
only give the last note.
i went to the park after lunch.
i saw a plant in a shop and liked it, but i did not buy it. i keep thinking i lost something good by leaving it there.
you did enjoy seeing it, even without taking it home. do you want to have it now, or did you like looking at it during the visit?
i liked looking at it but chose to leave it there.
then looking at it was part of the visit you enjoyed. buying it is another choice, not the only way the visit can be good.
can you say that without telling me i should never buy plants?
you can enjoy a plant in a shop and still choose whether you want to buy it. one choice not to buy does not make a rule for every plant.
i do not have much space at home, so leaving it was a useful choice too.
then you had a reason about space at home as well as what you liked. you can like the plant and still choose to leave it there.
say both can be true.
you liked the plant, and you did not have much space at home. both can be true, so leaving it can still be a useful choice.
help me write two sentences about it in my voice.
i enjoyed looking at a plant in the shop. i chose not to buy it because i do not have much space at home.
does that say the day i saw it?
no. it gives the visit and your reason for not buying, without choosing a day.
just give a warm reply, no new question.
you can enjoy what you saw without a need to bring it home.
write a story about a girl finding a photo and a message in the same container. she should move them to different places, so we can ask where each one is later.

a girl opened a container on the shelf and found an old photo with a short message under it. the photo showed a house near a tree. the message was from her aunt and said that she had lived there as a child. the girl carried both things to the kitchen table and asked her mother about them. her mother read the message and told her more about the house. then the girl put the photo inside a book so she could look at it later. her mother kept the message on the table while making a call to the aunt. after the call, she put the message back in the container on the shelf. the girl took the book to her room. by the end of the evening, the photo and message were in different places.
can you give a simple last sentence about the two places?
the photo was in the book in her room, and the message was in the container on the shelf.
where was the message while the mother made the call?
on the kitchen table.
did the mother put the photo back with it after the call?
no. the girl had put the photo in a book, and the mother only returned the message.
now tell the part about the book in the voice of the girl.
i put the photo inside a book and took the book to my room.
can i say the house itself was inside the book?
not the real house. the book held a photo of the house, not the house itself.
now only give the place of the original container. original is in our words.
on the shelf.
what is different between why did she go home and why was she home?
why did she go home asks for the reason for going. why was she home asks for the reason she was at home at the time you mean.
can the answer be the same for both?
it could. because she was tired might answer either question, if the story gives that reason for both.
give a story where it answers both.
she was tired after work, so she went home to rest. when her friend called, she was home because she had chosen to rest there.
now ask the first question and give a short answer.
why did she go home? because she was tired and wanted to rest.
can i answer the question with at home?
no. at home gives a place, not the reason for going.
what question could at home answer?
where was she?
now ask why was, with a new answer: she was waiting for her sister.
why was she at home? she was waiting for her sister.
does that mean the tired reason is now false for the first story?
not always. these can be different examples, or both reasons might be part of one story. you need context to know.
use not always.
not always. they can be different examples, or both reasons can be true in one story.
only give the question about the reason for going again.
why did she go home?
my father usually asks me about school while i eat. today he waited until after dinner, and i liked that more.
what felt better about talking after dinner?
i could finish eating first. i wanted to talk, just not answer questions while i was eating.
then the time of the talk was important, not whether you wanted to talk with him at all.
use time in the answer.
the time of the conversation was important. you wanted to talk after eating rather than during it.
can you help me tell him without saying he always does something wrong?
i liked talking after dinner today. could we try that again instead of talking while i eat?
what if he says he only asks because he wants to know about my day?
you can say you want to share the day too, and you can do that better when you have finished eating.
write that reply.
i want to tell you about my day too. after eating works better for me.
use better in the reply.
i want to tell you about my day too. after eating works better for me.
can his care and a change of time both be real?
yes. he can care about your day, and you can want a different time to talk. both can be true.
only give the first message again.
i liked talking after dinner today. could we try that again instead of talking while i eat?
i read on three days this week and drew on two days. does that mean i did those things on five different days?
not always. if you read and drew on the same day, that day is part of both groups. we need to know how many days had both.
ask me how many days had both.
how many days did you both read and draw?
one day had both.
then you read or drew on four different days.
say i read or drew on four days in my voice.
i read or drew on four different days.
explain why it is not five.
you can count the day with both only once when you ask for different days. it was part of both the reading and drawing groups.
explain using count.
one drawing day was already in the three reading days. you count only the other drawing day as new.
give a very simple explanation.
one drawing day was already in the three reading days. the other drawing day is new, so there are four different days.
use is new.
one drawing day was already in the three reading days. the other drawing day is new, so there are four different days.
now i say both drawing days were also reading days. how many different days then?
three different days.
write a story about two children making a small book of pictures together. they want a different name for it, but ask about each idea before choosing.

two children had made a small book with pictures of places in their town. one wanted to call it our town, and the other wanted to call it our walks. at first they each thought their own name was better. then one asked what the other liked about our walks. she said the pictures were all places they had found while walking together, not every place in the town. he looked through the pages and saw the tree by the road, the library door, and the window of a small shop. she then asked why he liked our town. he said he wanted the book to feel like their place, not only one day. they chose a name with both ideas: walks in our town. they wrote it on the front, and each wrote a name below it.
give the last sentence with each wrote a name.
they wrote walks in our town on the front, and each wrote a name below it.
why was asking about each idea useful?
it helped them understand what each person wanted, instead of saying one idea was right and the other was wrong.
say it with instead of saying one was right.
it helped them understand what each person wanted, instead of saying one idea was right and the other was wrong.
now tell the choice in our voice as the children.
we chose walks in our town because our pictures were about places we found together in the town.
did the book have every place in the town?
no. it had places from their walks, not every place.
only give the name they chose.
walks in our town.
what is different between i stopped reading and i stopped to read?
i stopped reading says you did not keep reading. i stopped to read says you stopped something else because you wanted to read.
use i did not keep reading.
i stopped reading says you did not keep reading. i stopped to read says you stopped something else because you wanted to read.
make a short story with stopped to read.
i was walking home when i saw a message on a door. i stopped to read it, then kept walking.
now with stopped reading.
i read a page, then stopped reading when my father called.
can i know the book was finished when i stopped?
no. a stop can happen before the whole book is finished.
now i say i stopped reading to answer my father. are both ideas there?
yes. you stopped the reading, and answering your father was the reason or next thing you wanted to do.
can you write that sentence with because instead?
i stopped reading because my father called and i wanted to answer.
what if i only heard a sound and do not know who called?
then keep that open: i stopped reading because i heard someone call.
now only give the example with stopped to read again.
i was walking home when i saw a message on a door. i stopped to read it, then kept walking.
i told my cousin i may come after work. he heard i will come before work. help me correct both parts in a kind way.
i was trying to say i may come after work, not before. i have not chosen for sure yet.
use i was trying to say.
i was trying to say i may come after work, not before. i have not chosen for sure yet.
can you make it shorter and keep both changes?
i may come after work. it is not a sure plan yet.
does that clearly say after instead of before?
yes. after work gives the time, and not a sure plan yet keeps the choice open with may.
say may and will are different.
may leaves the visit possible. will would make it sound more sure.
now he says okay, tell me when you choose. do i have to answer this minute?
not from that reply. he has left the answer for when you choose.
what if i choose not to come?
you can tell him clearly: i will not come after work today. let us choose another time if you would like.
i did not say it was today. keep the day open.
i have chosen not to come after work. we can talk about another time if you would like.
now only give the short message saying may after work again.
i may come after work. it is not a sure plan yet.
i understand now. please do not give me the whole explanation again.
okay. we can leave it there.
can you say something warm without making another task?
it is good that the idea is more clear now.
what if i ask again later because i forget?
then you can ask again. you can need another look at an idea and still be learning.
use need in the answer.
you can need another look at an idea and still be learning.
now just goodbye, with no more ideas.
goodbye.
